plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful deciduous tree that produces clouds of delicate, fragrant blossoms before its leaves emerge. It is the most celebrated cherry blossom cultivar and a centerpiece of spring festivals, planted widely in parks and along rivers and avenues.
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry trees around Washington D.C.'s Tidal Basin were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and their peak bloom date is closely tracked each year by the National Park Service.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers and slender blue-green leaves. It thrives in meadows, woodlands, and gardens, and is one of the most recognizable heralds of spring in temperate Europe.
plants.location: Western Europe, especially England, Wales, France, and Spain; widely naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain toxic alkaloids, but one of them, galantamine, is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia × soulangeana
plants.description: A small deciduous tree or large shrub bearing large, tulip-shaped goblet flowers on bare branches in early spring. It is a popular ornamental in gardens and streets across mild temperate climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid spring (March to April)
plants.location: Cultivated across the southeastern United States, the United Kingdom, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, having evolved before bees existed, and their flowers are thought to have been pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Though named for autumn, a close relative group in the Southern Hemisphere and autumn-flowering bulbs such as Sternbergia and Zephyranthes bloom now as the season turns there. Colchicum bears goblet-shaped lilac flowers that emerge directly from the ground without leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Northern Hemisphere; March flowering for Southern Hemisphere cultivated plantings with autumn bloom
plants.location: Cultivated in South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand; native to Europe
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used to treat gout and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.
